advances: Ordinary planar adjacent-edge ears whose base point lies in the closed double-signature interval.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $(n_j,c_j)=(v,x+s+w)$ for $j=2$ and $(v+w,x+s)$ for $j=3$, so $n_j+c_j=H$. For either case the cap $1$ and cap $l$ margins at $Q_0$ are $p-L\theta$ and $H\theta-n_j$. They are nonnegative on the stated interval. Its endpoints are strictly between zero and one, and $pH-n_j L\ge pH-(v+w)L=sp+vx>0$. The two diagonals cross at the relative interior point $Q_0$, so this is an actual quadrilateral. The new altitude from the base is $\varepsilon/k_0$ times the old one, giving exactly $\varepsilon$ extra area. The two affected margins at $P_j$ are strictly negative, so the displacement makes both affected peak margins strictly positive for $\varepsilon>0$, also at the endpoints. The cap $j$ margin on the added region is strictly negative.

For an ear triangle of area $E$ with base signed heights $a,-b$ for one cap, where $a,b>0$, and tip height $g\ge0$, the retained cap area and the coarea of its cut segment are
$$
E\left(1-\frac{b^2}{(a+b)(b+g)}\right),\qquad
\frac{2Eb}{(a+b)(b+g)} .
$$
The negative corner has edge fractions $b/(a+b)$ and $b/(b+g)$. Its volume is their product times $E$, and its Euclidean altitude from the cutting line is $b/\lVert v_i\rVert$, giving the segment formula. This argument also works for $g=0$, when the cutting segment ends at the tip.

Let $n=n_j$, $z=c_j$ in the derivative formulas below. The old positive and negative base heights in the two affected caps are $(p,-x)$ and $(z,-n)$, respectively. Their height sums with the zero-size peak are $x+(p-L\theta)=L(1-\theta)$ and $n+(H\theta-n)=H\theta$. Differentiating the clipping formulas at zero ear area gives
$$
Q_1'=1-\frac{x^2}{L^2(1-\theta)},\quad \sigma_1'=\frac{2x}{L^2(1-\theta)},\qquad
Q_l'=1-\frac{n^2}{H^2\theta},\quad \sigma_l'=\frac{2n}{H^2\theta}.
$$
Also $Q_j'=\sigma_j'=0$ and $k'=1$. The old data are those of the canonical coordinate lemma, in particular $Q_l=Lz^2/(2H)$ and $\sigma_l=Lz/H$. Logarithmic differentiation gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
M'&=\frac{p-L\theta}{(1-\theta)pB}+\frac{H\theta-n}{\theta Lz},\
D_j:=\Phi_1'&=(4-L/H)\left(\frac1{LB}-\frac{M'}H\right)
 +\frac LH\left(\frac{Q_1'}{2Q_1}-\frac{\sigma_1'}{\sigma_1}\right)
 +\frac BH\left(\frac{Q_l'}{2Q_l}-\frac{\sigma_l'}{\sigma_l}\right).
\end{aligned}
$$
Write $Z_j=pH-n_j L$, $\theta=n_j/H+u(p/L-n_j/H)$ for $u\in[0,1]$, and set $A_j=n_j L+uZ_j=HL\theta$, $B_j=Lc_j-uZ_j=HL(1-\theta)$ and $N_j=p^2c_j^2BLH^2 A_j B_j>0$. Define the following polynomials.
$$
\begin{aligned}
P_\star&=(2sp-x^{2}/4)^{2}+15x^{4}/16\\
&\quad +s(4w+2x)p^{2}+s x^{3}+p^{2}w(w+x)+vp x^{2}+(v+w)x^{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_+&=2s^{2}v+s^{2}w+s^{2}x+2svw+2svx+2sw^{2}+4swx+2sx^{2}\\
&\quad +vw^{2}+2vwx+vx^{2}+w^{3}+3w^{2}x+3wx^{2}+x^{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_-&=2s^{2}v+s^{2}w+s^{2}x+2svw+2svx+2sw^{2}+2sx^{2}\\
&\quad +vw^{2}+vx^{2}+w^{3}+x^{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_2&=40v^{3}w+32v^{3}x+60v^{2}w^{2}+64v^{2}wx+12v^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +30vw^{3}+44vw^{2}x+16vwx^{2}+2vx^{3}+5w^{4}+10w^{3}x+5w^{2}x^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_2&=32v^{3}w^{2}+44v^{3}wx+16v^{3}x^{2}+48v^{2}w^{3}+84v^{2}w^{2}x\\
&\quad +44v^{2}wx^{2}+8v^{2}x^{3}+24vw^{4}+55vw^{3}x+42vw^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +15vwx^{3}+4vx^{4}+4w^{5}+12w^{4}x+12w^{3}x^{2}+4w^{2}x^{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
G_2&=(w+x)\bigl[8v^{3}w^{2}+8v^{3}wx+4v^{3}x^{2}+12v^{2}w^{3}+18v^{2}w^{2}x\\
&\quad +10v^{2}wx^{2}+4v^{2}x^{3}+6vw^{4}+13vw^{3}x+10vw^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +5vwx^{3}+2vx^{4}+w^{5}+3w^{4}x+3w^{3}x^{2}+w^{2}x^{3}\bigr].
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_3&=8v^{3}w+32v^{3}x+12v^{2}w^{2}+56v^{2}wx+12v^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +6vw^{3}+36vw^{2}x+8vwx^{2}+2vx^{3}+w^{4}+8w^{3}x+w^{2}x^{2}+2wx^{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_3&=x\bigl[20v^{3}w+16v^{3}x+40v^{2}w^{2}+28v^{2}wx+8v^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +29vw^{3}+18vw^{2}x+5vwx^{2}+4vx^{3}+7w^{4}+4w^{3}x+w^{2}x^{2}+4wx^{3}\bigr].
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
G_3&=x\bigl[4v^{3}w^{2}+4v^{3}wx+4v^{3}x^{2}+10v^{2}w^{3}+8v^{2}w^{2}x\\
&\quad +6v^{2}wx^{2}+4v^{2}x^{3}+8vw^{4}+7vw^{3}x+2vw^{2}x^{2}\\
&\quad +5vwx^{3}+2vx^{4}+2w^{5}+2w^{4}x+2w^{2}x^{3}+2wx^{4}\bigr].
\end{aligned}
$$

Put $R_j=2s^3p^2L+s^2E_j+sF_j+G_j$, $C_{j0}=n_j^2c_j^2L^2P_\star$, $C_{j1}=pc_j LHR_j/2$, $C_{22}=x^2p^2H^3P_+$ and $C_{32}=x^2p^2H^3P_-$. Clearing denominators in the displayed expression for $D_j$ gives the identity
$$
-N_jD_j=C_{j0}(1-u)^2+2C_{j1}u(1-u)+C_{j2}u^2.
$$
The completed square and $15x^4/16$ give $P_\star>0$. The leading term of $R_j$ is strictly positive and every monomial in its displayed supplements is nonnegative. Both $P_+$ and $P_-$ have the term $x^3>0$. Thus every Bernstein coefficient is strictly positive on the parameter domain including $w=0$, and the identity gives $D_j<0$ for all $u\in[0,1]$.

At the old triangle write $r=f_1$ and $z=f_2=f_3$. Then $r+z^2=2$, $0<z^2<2$, and
$$
4\bigl(2-z-(r+z)^2/4\bigr)=(4-z^2)(z-1)^2.
$$
If $z\ne1$, rows $2$ and $3$ are initially strict and remain so by continuity. If $z=1$, all $f_i=1$ initially and the three row derivatives all equal $f_1'+f_2'+f_3'$. Thus a strictly negative derivative in row $1$ gives all three strict inequalities for sufficiently small positive ear size in either case.
statement:
For a planar convex body $K$ containing $0$ in its interior and three nonzero spanning normals $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$, write
$$
k=|K|,\qquad Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|,\qquad
\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert .
$$
Set $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$ and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ where $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$. A triangle has strict distinct-vertex incidence if cap $i$ contains its vertex $P_i$ in its open halfplane and excludes both other vertices strictly.

Use the normals $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$. The canonical vertices for row $1$ are
$$
P_1=(2v+w,-v-w),\qquad P_2=(-x,x+s),\qquad P_3=(-x,-s-w),
\qquad x,s,v>0,\quad w\ge0.
$$

Write $p=2v+w$, $L=x+p$, $H=x+s+w+v$, $B=x+2s+w$ and $k_0=LB/2$. For $j=2,3$ write $l$ for the other index in $\{2,3\}$, and put $n_2=v$, $n_3=v+w$. For each fixed $\theta\in[n_j/H,p/L]$ and $Q_0=(1-\theta)P_1+\theta P_l$, set
$$
Q_\varepsilon=Q_0+(\varepsilon/k_0)(Q_0-P_j),\qquad
K_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(P_1,P_2,P_3,Q_\varepsilon).
$$
For $\varepsilon>0$ this is a quadrilateral adding area $\varepsilon$ along $P_1P_l$. The right derivative of $\Phi_1$ at zero is strictly negative, and all three rows are strict for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$.
title: Strict Lorentz first variation for the two adjacent-edge ears
